x: In the Invitation Mile, John Davies was 6th in 4mins. 12 secs. an excellent performance, and as stated previously Stan Vickers was 2nd and Ted Smith 4th in a two miles walk.
Our rapidly improving miler, J. Davies gave us another first place in the mile and Tooby and Baulch finished 2nd and 3rd respectively in the 2 miles.
Outstanding recollections of the meeting were a fine sprint double by Ivan Mayers, some grand half miling by J. Davies (1m.57.8) and B. Hallowell (1m.59) and a very good half mile by Charlie Dabbs.

Our greatest thrill however was to note the running of John Davies in the International 800 metres event. He had been invited to turn up as a reserve and found himself stripped off in a field of eight which included Moens of Belgium, the World's record holder at this distance, Brian Hewson, Britain'…

On May 24th John Davies was selected for the A.A.A. v Cambridge University and on a grass track at Fenners, won the mile in 14m. 12.6s. Ivan Mayers was also in the team and was placed 3rd in the 100 yards and was a member of the winning Relay team.
Our Middlesex men also had their share of the spoils, the most outstanding being J. Davies who won the mile in 4m. 17.8s. on a very dusty and windy track.

The mile saw John Davies in the line up but sad to relate he did not benefit from his poor track tactics on Friday and although he made an effort to make up lost ground, Clark had again opened up a lead and John was forced back to 5th place in 4.13.8, the winner eventually being J.
Our 440 strength is definitely getting stronger as there were two heats before the final. The 880 yards was won by John Davies in 1min. 56.8s.
We had but one entry in the 880 yards, but John Davies was destined to give us our greatest thrill by qualifying for the final in a time of 1.52.8, a new club best performance.
Our John Davies and Brian Hallowell ran with rare judgment and proved that with wise training they are capable of giving the best a run for their money.
In the Sefton Branker Trophy Meeting on 25th July Brian Hallowell representing the Civil Service was 2nd in the mile and John Davies (Middlesex) was 3rd.
John Davies won the 800 metres in 1m.57.6s. whilst Gerry Leroy was unlucky not get into the final. Newell and Stroud were 4th. and 7th. respectively in the 1500 metres, Newell's time being 3m.58s.

Dennis gave us the lead but Pat Fox, inexperienced as he was, lost ground and handed over to John Davies 40yds. down. John set about his task in workmanlike style, running in his usual relaxed way, he reduced the lead on the first lap and in the back straight of the final lap came away to give us a win.
The next leg was a new one of little more than two miles in length and John Davies, complete with an arm in plaster following a fracture, was entrusted with it.

John Davies, who has been a regular participant in cross country fixtures this year, led home the Belgrave contingent in 8th place, closely followed by a pack of Belgravians in 10th, 11th, 12th, 14th, 15th, 17th and 18th positions.

Some great running has come from Brian Morris, with a 48·9s. quarter to his credit when representing the South against the North and Midlands and from John Davies (4m.10·6s.) for Middlesex versus Cambridge.

Although entries were only average in number a very fine Championship meeting was held and some really excellent performances were witnessed. Outstanding amongst these were the doubles of Clive Ryan in the 100 and 220 yds. and John Davies in the 880yds and 1 mile.

However, John Davies and Pat Newell came to the rescue with two very fine efforts, John finishing second to Gordon Pirie in the 1500 metres with a time of 3m.59 1s. and Pat chased John Disley home in the 3 miles to finish less than two seconds behind in 14m.39 6s. and incidently beat Langridge of S.…

There were, however, some good individual performances by Club members and the following are on record:- 440 yds in 49.6s. by Brian Morris, 1 mile in 4m.11.6s. by John Davies and a 5'10" high jump and a 21'10½" long jump by Mal Ash.

Two Championships, three handicaps and an inter-schools relay were decided at Battersea Park on the above occasion. The main event was the Club 3 miles Championship for the Griffin Cup in which John Davies surprisingly, but decisively, beat P.
John Davies won both the half and one mile in 1m.57 6s. and 4m.23s. respectively, while Brian Morris had a narrow win in the 220 with a time of 22 7s.
This was a triangular affair involving ourselves, Cambridge Harriers and Herne Hill Harriers and once again John Davies won both the 880 yds. and 1 mile although the times were only moderate.

John Davies had the shortest trip of the day (hardly worth the bother of changing John!) and at Salfords Woodford had taken over from Pompey, we had improved slightly and were now three minutes and twenty seconds in arrears; it was felt that this was still too large a gap.
Brian Morris and John Davies have already recorded good times for the 440 yds. and 1500 metres respectively, whilst Alan Black and Malcolm Robinson look set for their best seasons yet.

Meanwhile John Davies and Jim Heathfield were doing battle with a string of Blackheath men a little further back. Both of our boys lost ground on the dangerous stretches with a sensible "safety first" policy but made it up in the last mile or so of even going; John, in particular, gaining several places.

Unfortunately, for a variety of reasons, Archie Bedford, John Davies, Colin Collis and Clive Shippen were unable to run, so with six to score and a "12 cup" in the offing we were able to start nine only.
John Davies performed well to do 18.40 on the fourth lap and maintained his position although losing some ground to the leaders who were then over a minute ahead.

The tale of woe really began during the week prior to the race when firstly John Davies was forced to withdraw because of foot trouble and then Clive Shippen contracted enteritis and had to stand down.

Brian Morris and John Davies showed their class by cantering home in the 440 and 880 respectively and virtually clinched the match for us. An excellent start to the season was made by Norman Caves in the triple jump with 45'4", only 13" less than his highly ranked best of last year.

Our own John Davies, Brian Morris, Clive Ryan, Frank Wright and D. McCorquindale were competing elsewhere, and with Stan Vickers Eric Hall, Norman Caves, Mal Ash and Andorka also unavailable our team could not be said to be truly representative of the name of Belgrave.

In the Middlesex Championships at Enfield Dave Ansell was once more amongst the leading long jumpers and finished second with 21'5¼". John Davies, holder of the mile title, was unable to compete owing to other commitments.
John Davies showed a most welcome return to form in the 1 mile turning the tables on Mal Robinson - his victor in the Club Champs., with 4:13.7 for 4th place, as against Mal's 4:19 for 9th.

John Davies was not at his best on this occasion and had to be content with a mile time of 4:16.8. The Midland Champs. were held on the same day with Peter Eldridge performing excellently in both the 220 and 440 yards.
It was here that John Davies, only a little further back, was brought to a standstill by an attack of stomach cramp and could only finish at a trot.
John Davies, moved up from the 'B' team to take Clive Shippen's place, soon had Marlow of Highgate breathing down his neck and at halfway was forced to relinquish the lead.

In the final stages of the mile it looked very much as though Belgrave were, for the first time, going to finish both their runners in the first six; but although Mal Robinson clung to his fifth spot and a personal best of 4:15.2, John Davies had to give ground and with 4:17.1 finished seventh.

John Davies in an attempt to push Alan through to a fast time ran to the ¾ mile mark with 64, 2:12, 3:18, but although Alan had little left for a fast last lap, he broke the tape a clear winner in 4:27.8.

With half a lap to go in the 880yds, defending champion John Davies looked an odds-on winner, but in the final straight first Terry Newell and then Dave Mitchell sprinted past, leaving a surprised John to finish fourth just behind Bhatia who had made up a tremendous amount of ground in the last 220yds.
Erases two names from the record list--Brian Hallowell and John Davies at 4:10.6. Ranjit now has the honour of being Asia's fastest miler.

The strength of every team is governed by its weakest man, but with experienced men like Charlie Walker, John Davies and Eric Gebbett to complete our teams it is difficult to see where our weakest link can lie.
John Davies, pursuing his even-paced running theme, gained another place to 8th, but his time of 18.45 was below the standard we would expect from a man of his capabilities.
Haith and Herring, who took their clubs well away, but he held off the remainder - handing over to John Davies in third place with Reading 11 seconds behind.
JOHN DAVIES brings the BELS. home in 5th place after passing BLACKPOOL and BRISTOL in the last half-mile.

Others to set up personal bests in this event are Malcolm Robinson with 9:08.2, Pat Newell 9:09, Dan Maclean 9:11.6 and John Davies 9:15. Malcolm, who lost his club mile title to John, is the fastest miler so far this season with 4:12.2, set in the Southern Championships, Bill Kerr is second with 4:16.0.
Our two single point donations came from a jaded looking John Davies in the 1500 metres (4 minutes 1.6) and from that all-round field event man, George Edwards, with a 9'6" pole-vault.
For two laps the holder, Malcolm Robinson, led the field through the elements until Don Maclean took over with Pat Newell and John Davies on his heels.

John Davies, Ron Linstead and Alan Black ran the next three stages all within 15 secs. of each other, and although we dropped two places we were still within striking distance of second place - as Bill Kerr showed only too well!
Lower down the field John Davies and Cyril Forey were running together - the former running within his obvious capabilities, the latter short of training and feeling his way carefully.
STAGE 6 - John Davies (13:59 4th ) John did not produce the performance of which we all know he is capable. In the past year or so he has seemed afraid to really let himself go.
John Davies set a fast pace on the first stage, taking the field up a half-mile of steep hill, in good form, but faded somewhat in the middle stages.
Fortunately this alone did not quite decide the result. Charlie Walker and John Davies backed up well, with 6 to score we would have won.

On the way out to the village John Davies led the field whilst in the bunch behind a few private battles were taking place. (I understand that at this stage a man named Penney was causing some comment by being in a forward position in the field) At the end of the first lap Barry Sawyer had opened up…

John Davies had held a good lead after the first of the three 2½ mile laps and appeared to be in great form but an acute attack of stitch forced him to stop for a time and lose considerable ground and places.
Excellent support also came from Barry Sawyer, Eric Gebbett and John Davies but it is difficult to accurately assess the future of these three.
Bill Kerr and John Davies got away well and after the first half mile were contesting the lead whilst our other runners were all well-placed.
In coming 7th John Davies set up a club record by going slightly off-course on Wimbledon Common for the second time this winter, whilst leading.

John Davies on leg 6 also held on to fifth place but was a little disappointing. John's capabilities never really come to light in this sort of event and with his basic turn of speed he should be able to do 18 mins, for this lap, but lack of confidence in his own powers seems to be his biggest enemy.

STAGE I - John Davies (21:16, 13th fastest) The first leg was led home by Hammond of Coventry (2nd in this year's National Youths Cross-country) with John lagging 55 seconds behind having lost touch before Chelsea Bridge.

John Thresher and John Davies produced fine efforts to beat Barratt of Ealing in the mile clocking 4:24.4 and 4:25.7 respectively. As can be seen already, conditions were certainly not conducive to fast times.
John Davies just failed to hold Blagrove of Ealing in the 2 miles and finished 10 yards down with 9:31.9.
Nobody would have given very long odds on John Thresher and sure enough, he lived up to his form by 'taking' John Davies down the finishing straight.

John Davies beat Don Maclean in a tussle for second place with O'Hara closing on them at the finish. The most encouraging feature of this event was the number of 'lesser lights' who got inside sixteen minutes and showed that we have certain strength in depth.

Jack Brown and John Davies were our fastest 'B' men, but special mention should be made of young Tony Fairclough, who recorded an excellent 14:05 and of Cyril Forey whose 13:59 for the 'C' team may have seemed bad selection - in fact he had been in training for but 3 weeks after a 5 month lay off an…

Then we had John Davies producing the form of which we know he is capable to take the fastest time of the day on the 6th stage. Also Pat Newell returned to the team to record another first-class performance and so lower the Belgrave record for the 10th stage by 13 secs.

John Davies consolidated our second place and John Thresher took us into the lead at the half way mark. "Charlie boy" didn't look very happy leading Stage 4 with the result that Don Maclean took over with opponents hard on his heels.

Jack Brown had to make full use of his experience to pull back Tony Fairclough and John Davies in the later stages but eventually he got away from them and was fast catching Barry Sawyer in the run in.

TOP RIGHT: Laurie O'Hara gives Gerry North the lead we all hoped for---46 secs over Portsmouth after 7 stages. John Davies, behind, takes a time-check. CENTRE LEFT: That long stretch of empty road behind Gerry North lengthens with every stride.
Trevor Hart, showing a welcome return to form, and John Davies maintained sixth position quite comfortably. Belgrave 'B' team finished fifteenth, Pat Sadler having a good run with 10m 24s.

Granted our best dozen runners were not competing - because of the Johnstone Relay the following day - but the efforts by Linstead, Satchell and our"prodigal son" John Davies should keep the first team men on their toes.

Don was beaten on the tape by John Davies, with Newall 3rd and Robinson 4th. In his last track season at Oxford he made a big effort to gain a 'blue' but, despite an all time personal best of 4:14.7,he was unsuccessful.

I can see down there from our colony in the South Seas - George Piddington - and fresh from his long retirement - John Davies ... the whistle goes, they are under starters orders ... suddenly the sun comes out on to the rain sodden track ...
That husband and wife athletic team JOHN and PAM DAVIES are expecting their first-born on December 27th. If it should prove to be a boy, John promises to sign him up for Belgrave immediately.
A good run apiece by these two established stars was backed by the new veteran's star Brian Gorman, while John Davies made a welcome appearance to lead in the second wave of Bels.

Beverley, now 35, recorded 2:48:46, only 27 minutes behind the winner. - What about that John Davies? We note that the ladies of the MacLean family have signed up in force.
John Davies ran a creditable 2:58:51 and Georgie Piddington raced to his best ever '20' 2:26 and then carried on to 3:23:21 for the full distance.

A little way back John Davies and Paul Pringle were keeping each other company, and John Baker and Dave Drake were steadily plodding away. By 20 km positions were much the same with the effects of the heat beginning to show.
John Davies was also making good progress through the field having set himself a target before the race of 2:08 - such pace judgement is remarkable.

In the Unigate Marathon at Harlow four Bels were among the 256 starters and were led home by John Davies who ran an even paced race to finish strongly at 96th in 2:53:21.

Only three competitors from Belgrave figured on the Mitcham 25 Kilometre result sheet, preferring 15 miles plus on the road to the vagaries of the Common and our 10 mile cross country championship. Pat O'Connor was 34th in 86:20, with Stew Barrett 84th, 94:10, and John Davies 89th, 95:05.

Of the Bels, Lionel Mann retained the Belgrave Championship from Bill Laws (a silver medal at his first '20' attempt) and John Davies. Thanks as usual must go to all the regular marksmen, recorders, refreshment post stewards, timekeepers and results team who helped make the afternoon a success.
